newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down slightly in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down slightly in listless trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mostly slightly lower in listless trade with July as the front month, industry sources said.

"Coming into the first day of trade with July as the front month, it's pretty dead," said one New York-based futures trader, adding "forecasts are calling for some cooler weather in the Southwest and natural gas is pretty much unchanged."

As of 1245 EDT, July Palo Verde (PV) was down 37 cents at $30.85 after exchanges in a range of $30.35-30.90, while August was 37 cents lower at $32.10 following exchanges at $32.00-32.30 per megawatt hour (MWh).
July California Oregon Border (COB) was off one cent at $23.10 after exchanges at $22.75-23.35, while August was down 35 cents at the day's high of $26.10 after reaching as low as $26.00 per MWh.
Trade volumes were not immediately available from NYMEX.
As of 1235 EDT, June NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas was down 0.7 cents at $2.356 per million British thermal units.
Separately, restart of the 1,087 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear plant in central California has been delayed until the weekend.
The which has been shut for scheduled refueling since April 19, had been expected to begin delivering power to the regional grid Thursday.

Arizona Public Service said it expects to restore output at the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit Wednesday night. Palo Verde 1 was in a hot standby mode as of early Wednesday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.

A total of about 7,000 megawatts of power generation remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance. However, much of the idled generation was expected to return to service over the next several weeks.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be near or just below normal through the week, then rising to four to eight degrees above normal on the weekend.
In Seattle, temperatures were expected to reach a maximum o 67 degrees Fahrenheit Thursday, with a low near 51 degrees.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be three to seven degrees above normal through into the early weekend across the extreme south and west. To the north and east, temperatures were expected to be near to slightly above normal through into the weekend.
In Phoenix, Ariz., temperatures were expected to reach a maximum near 96 degrees Wednesday with lows expected near 70 degrees.
COB open interest for May 27 fell 175 to 5,464 while PV open interest rose 18 to 6,327, NYMEX said.
